Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Africa Congo confirms Ebola outbreak has spread to eighth province Source : Reuters 19 October 2026 12:12am There are currently no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola but some have been trialed. Audio By Carbonatix
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has spread to ​an eighth province, North Ubangi, Congo's public ‌health institute said on Sunday, confirming earlier Reuters reporting.
The emergence of cases in the province bordering the Central African Republic poses a new challenge for health authorities struggling to contain the outbreak.
The National ⁠Institute for Biomedical Research confirmed two cases - ​including one death - in North Ubangi.
Reuters reported on Thursday that ​two cases were confirmed in the province, citing two health officials. At the time, there was no official statement ​by Congolese authorities.
North Ubangi becomes the eighth province affected by the outbreak, alongside North Kivu, Ituri, Haut-Uele, Tshopo, Sud-Kivu, Bas-Uele, and South Ubangi.
The outbreak, the worst Ebola epidemic in Congo's history, has already spread beyond the country's borders, with cases recorded in Uganda ​and seven infections confirmed ​in Kenya ⁠this month.
Congo's latest situation report showed 67 new confirmed cases and 26 new deaths in the 24 hours to Oct.16, bringing the cumulative total to 9,415 cases and 4,536 deaths since the outbreak began.
The outbreak remains concentrated in eastern Congo, with Ituri province accounting for 44 of the 67 new cases.
